findings.title: Polygon's publicnode endpoint answers from at least five unpublished bor commits and rotates between two of them within minutes
findings.difference: Ethereum endpoints serve tagged client releases. polygon-bor-rpc.publicnode.com, the RPC that networks.json lists for Polygon, reported bor/cb3d19c5f690/v2.11.1-private at 09:15 UTC and bor/280514fa9fb7/v2.11.1-private at 09:23 and 09:26 UTC on 2026-11-26. Neither commit, nor the three seen in earlier cycles, exists on raw.githubusercontent.com.
findings.mechanism: An eth_call answer from this endpoint can come from either private build. The battery and the targeted set ran unpinned against it and matched every vector, so both builds in rotation during the run compute the opcodes the pool math uses as specified. No source can be read for them, so a change to core/vm in either build is known only through its answers.
findings.impact: No loss. Results from this endpoint cannot be tied to one build unless each batch is bracketed with web3_clientVersion.
findings.preconditions: Only the endpoint operator decides which build serves a request.
findings.mitigations: Pin opcode and script runs to a build string, or use an endpoint that reports a tagged release such as QuikNode's v2.11.1 builds.

So FullMath.mulDiv, BitMath, TickMath, SqrtPriceMath and TickBitmap get the same results there as on Ethereum.

cleared.check: bor's MULMOD memo (v2.12.0-beta and develop, core/vm/mulmod_memo.go) read against holiman/uint256 v1.3.2, for the two moduli FullMath.mulDiv uses on one call (2^256-1 at FullMath.sol:24, then the denominator at FullMath.sol:48).
cleared.result: The memo keys on the full four-limb modulus (mm.mod != *z), copies it before the in-place write, and calls MulModWithReciprocal, which in v1.3.2 (uint256.go:688-715) is MulMod (uint256.go:720-748) with the reciprocal passed in. Zero operands return 0 before the reciprocal is used. Alternating moduli only cause misses. The result is a pure function of the three operands. No reachable endpoint runs it yet.

cleared.result: Cargo.lock of 23b510f and v0.1.4 pin the same revm, revm-interpreter, revm-handler, revm-context, revm-precompile, revm-bytecode, revm-state and ruint versions. cleared.check: The SAE executor of avalanchego 1.15.3 read for transaction boundaries and the EVM it runs.
cleared.result: Execute (saexec/execution.go:293-470) sets the transaction context and runs core.ApplyTransaction once per transaction on one StateDB. ApplyTransaction prepares and finalises state per transaction, which clears transient storage. The interpreter is libevm with vm.Config{}, the same one eth_call uses. End-of-block atomic operations run after all transactions and change only AVAX balances. So the unlock flag, the deltas and the synced currency (Lock.sol:13-25, CurrencyReserves.sol:17-36) live for one transaction as on Ethereum.

cleared.check: Whether a public account can cause a reorganisation or profit from one against a PoolManager user, including replay of a settled or taken transaction in another order (lead L-1046).
cleared.result: A reorganisation needs block producers on all three networks: bor producers and Heimdall milestones, BSC validators with BEP-126 votes, Avalanche validators under Snowman. A re-included transaction keeps its signature and nonce and runs once. Its unlock is atomic (PoolManager.sol:104-114), so a take without a matching settle reverts whatever the order. A different order can change the price a swap gets, which is the ordinary ordering risk that slippage limits in routers handle. Only the owner or fee controller can change the protocol fee, and only a pool's own hook can change its dynamic fee, so a replay cannot pay more than the pool's state at that position gives.

The memo is always on there and the widened keccak cache needs EnablePrecompileCache. The rerun after block 98,688,600 cannot happen before the fork.

Recorded as refused, not worked around. polygon-bor-rpc.publicnode.com answers historical log and state requests with HTTP 403 'Archive requests require a personal token', and bsc-rpc.publicnode.com returns a Cloudflare challenge page. On Avalanche, avalanche-c-chain-rpc.publicnode.com answered the first window but refused this client with HTTP 403 three times from the second window on, so the run was stopped and recorded as refused (gap43114.log); api.avax.network answered every window it was asked. The other networks in the lead belong to other units.

Both forks are 12 days away. Build strings on 2026-11-26: bsc-dataseed1 rotates Geth/v1.8.2 (no commit) and v1.8.2-4e1c8247, both of which pass the full pinned battery and targeted set; bsc-rpc.publicnode.com refuses this client; polygon-bor-rpc.publicnode.com rotates bor cb3d19c5f690 and 280514fa9fb7, both v2.11.1-private, and passes unpinned. The five Salvador accounts have no code today, and Salvador gives them sweeper code that sends their own native balance to a fixed recovery address. The PoolManager reaches an address only when a caller names it in take or sync, or as a pool currency or hook. Cycle 21 found none of the five used as a pool currency. The post-fork rerun is owed.

Polygon: finalized lagged latest by two blocks and safe is not served. Polygon had a milestone fork on 10 September 2025 (some providers rewound to block 76,273,070), a span rotation fault on 17 December 2025 and a finality halt on 12 January 2026, all caused by producer and Heimdall code. BSC: BEP-126 finalizes with two justified blocks, and finalized lagged by one or two. Avalanche: Snowman acceptance is final, and under SAE safe and finalized trail latest by six blocks because they mark settled execution. A reorganisation needs producers on all three. A re-included transaction keeps its nonce and its unlock is atomic (PoolManager.sol:104-114). Protocol fees need the controller and dynamic fees need the pool's hook, so a different order changes only the swap price, which router slippage limits bound.
